01 · Septic tanks

2026 EPA septic tank inspections: 59% failed

5 November 2026 · NB Hydro Logistics · Dublin, Ireland

59%of inspected septic tanks failed in 2025
€12,000maximum remediation grant
5 yearskeep desludging receipts

The EPA's latest report shows almost six in ten inspected septic tanks failing. If you have a septic tank in Dublin, Fingal, South Dublin, Dún Laoghaire–Rathdown, Wicklow, Kildare or Meath, here is what the 2026 picture means for you.

What the EPA found

Local authorities completed 1,466 septic tank inspections in 2025 and 863 of them (59%) failed. The most common reasons are inadequate desludging and maintenance, plus structural defects such as leaks, ponding, rainwater ingress and illegal discharges to ditches or streams. Fingal was one of three authorities that fell short of its inspection target and has to make up the shortfall in 2026, so Dublin homeowners should expect inspectors to be active.

Grants of up to €12,000

The remediation grant was raised from €5,000 to €12,000 in 2024. Eligibility and the application process are set by the Department of Housing, Local Government and Heritage, so check the current criteria before you start any works. A tank that fails inspection gets an advisory notice from the local authority setting out what has to be fixed.

Keep your desludging records for five years

Councils advise owners to use an authorised waste collector for every desludge and to keep the receipt for five years. An inspector will normally ask for it first, and it is the simplest proof that your tank is being maintained.

Septic tank desludging in Dublin

NB Hydro empties domestic, farm and commercial septic tanks and treatment systems across Dublin and surrounding counties, takes the waste to authorised facilities and gives you the paperwork for your records.

Key points
  • Desludge at least once a year, or as your system manual advises
  • Use a collector with a valid waste collection permit
  • Keep receipts and servicing records together
  • Fix any advisory notice within the timeframe given
  • Ask about grants before starting repair works

02 · Compliance

NWCPO permit compliance and the €5,000 fine risk

5 November 2026 · NB Hydro Logistics · Dublin, Ireland

Mandatorypermit for every commercial waste collector
€5,000maximum fine on summary conviction
nwcpo.iecheck any collector before you book

Anyone who collects and transports waste commercially in Ireland must hold a valid waste collection permit from the National Waste Collection Permit Office (NWCPO). That covers septic tank sludge, grease trap waste, interceptor contents and industrial wastewater.

Who needs a permit

The requirement comes from the Waste Management Act 1996 and the Waste Management (Collection Permit) Regulations. If waste is collected as part of a business, the collector needs a permit, the permit must cover the type of waste being carried, and it must be carried on the vehicle.

The €5,000 fine and what sits behind it

Unauthorised disposal of waste carries a maximum fine of €5,000 on summary conviction and/or up to 12 months in prison, and up to €15 million and/or 10 years on conviction on indictment. Enforcement is carried out by local authorities and the Office of Environmental Enforcement.

Your duty as a customer

Householders, landlords, farmers and businesses are expected to hand waste only to authorised collectors. Before you book any tanker service in Dublin, search the collector on nwcpo.ie, ask to see a copy of the permit, confirm it covers your waste type and keep the receipt or waste docket.

Why it matters in Dublin

Dublin's dense drainage network means illegal tipping can reach rivers and the Liffey estuary quickly. Using a permitted contractor protects you, your property and local water quality.

Key points
  • Search the collector on nwcpo.ie
  • Ask to see the permit and check the waste type is covered
  • Keep receipts and waste dockets
  • Never accept a cash deal with no paperwork
  • Report suspected illegal dumping to your local authority

03 · Agriculture

Slurry storage rules 2026: S.I. 588/2025 & S.I. 119/2026

5 November 2026 · NB Hydro Logistics · Dublin, Ireland

S.I. 588/2025Good Agricultural Practice Regulations 2025
S.I. 119/20262026 amendment to the 2025 Regulations
2026–2028Sixth Nitrates Action Programme

Farmers in Dublin, Meath, Kildare and Wicklow are working to new nitrates rules. S.I. No. 588 of 2025 gives legal effect to Ireland's Sixth Nitrates Action Programme, and S.I. No. 119 of 2026 amends it.

S.I. 588/2025: the Good Agricultural Practice Regulations

The European Union (Good Agricultural Practice for Protection of Waters) Regulations 2025 revoke the earlier regulations and apply to all holdings, including the movement and spreading of organic and chemical fertiliser. They sit alongside the Sixth Nitrates Action Programme, which runs from 2026 to 2028.

S.I. 119/2026: what changed

The 2026 amendment alters several articles and schedules of the 2025 Regulations and inserts new provisions, including a new Schedule 5. Read the consolidated text on irishstatutebook.ie or ask your adviser, because the amendments change how some of the 2025 rules apply.

Storage, buffer zones and records

The programme increases slurry and soiled water storage requirements, with a longer lead-in for dairy farms, so review your capacity now rather than at the last minute. Whichever rules apply to your holding, keep records of slurry movements and spreading and respect buffer zones near watercourses and wells.

Slurry removal and transport

NB Hydro provides tanker capacity for slurry removal and transfer to farms across Dublin and surrounding counties, using permitted vehicles and keeping records of every load.

Key points
  • Confirm storage capacity for your stocking rate and zone
  • Respect buffer zones near watercourses and wells
  • Record slurry movements and spreading
  • Use only permitted contractors for transport
  • Check the consolidated S.I. 588/2025 as amended by S.I. 119/2026

High-pressure jetting & CCTV surveys for Dublin sewer blockages

5 November 2026 · NB Hydro Logistics · Dublin, Ireland

Fastblockage clearance with jetting
CCTVsee the real condition of the pipe
Reportclear findings and next steps

A recurring blockage is rarely random. In Dublin, ageing pipework, tree roots, grease and fat build-up and collapsed sections are the usual causes. Jetting clears the symptom and a CCTV survey finds the cause.

How high-pressure water jetting works

A specialist nozzle fires water jets against the pipe wall, breaking up grease, scale, silt and debris and flushing it towards the tanker, where it is vacuumed out. It suits domestic drains, commercial kitchens, car parks, gullies, manholes and mainline sewers.

Why add a CCTV drain survey

A camera shows the real condition of the pipe: cracks, displaced joints, root ingress, misconnections and collapses. You get a clear record for insurers, landlords, property sales and planning, and you can confirm the line is clear after jetting.

Common Dublin problems

Older terraces in Dublin City and Dún Laoghaire–Rathdown often have shared or combined drains, while new developments in Fingal and South Dublin can suffer from construction debris. Restaurants and hotels across the city centre regularly face fat build-up.

Prevent the next blockage

Scheduled maintenance jetting and periodic surveys cost far less than emergency call-outs, flooding or lost trading time. We can set up a regular programme for your property.

Key points
  • Locate the exact position of the blockage
  • Clear grease, silt, scale and roots
  • Inspect the pipe with CCTV before and after
  • Plan repairs before a collapse happens
  • Recorded findings for insurers and landlords

Commercial wastewater & interceptor sludge handling in Dublin

5 November 2026 · NB Hydro Logistics · Dublin, Ireland

Interceptorsoil and petrol separators
Grease trapsrestaurants, hotels, commercial kitchens
Paperworkwaste records for your compliance file

Garages, car washes, food producers, hotels, depots and industrial units across Dublin have to keep interceptors, grease traps and wastewater systems working and dispose of the sludge lawfully.

What is interceptor sludge

Oil and petrol interceptors capture hydrocarbons and solids before water reaches the sewer. The sludge and oily water they hold must be removed regularly and, depending on the contents, may be classed as hazardous waste.

Trade effluent and legal responsibility

Businesses discharging non-domestic wastewater to a public sewer may need authorisation from Uisce Éireann. As the waste producer you stay responsible for the waste until it reaches a lawful facility, so use a permitted collector and keep your waste documentation.

A sensible servicing plan

Match the servicing frequency to your site rather than waiting for an alarm or a smell. Inspect and empty interceptors on a fixed schedule, clean grease traps before they overflow, jet connecting pipework during servicing and file the waste transfer documents for audits.

Commercial tanker services

NB Hydro collects and transports commercial and industrial wastewater and sludge in Dublin and nearby counties, and supplies the paperwork your compliance file needs.

Key points
  • Interceptor and grease trap emptying and cleaning
  • Industrial wastewater and sludge removal
  • Jetting of connecting pipework
  • Waste transported by permitted vehicles
  • Records for audits and inspections
